key_insight: UNSM altered the local hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with DS and HVOF deposits showing different hardness ranges and peak conditions.
engineering_relevance: The study helps guide post-spray surface enhancement strategies for wear-resistant coatings by linking process route and UNSM settings to near-surface mechanical response.
method: Detonation-sprayed (DS) and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were post-processed by UNSM.
Four samples per route were tested at 20/30 N static loads and 20/30 µm vibration amplitudes.
Hardness was measured by instrumented indentation at 300 mN with a 10 s dwell; scratch-induced surface morphology was examined by SEM.
evidence_signal: DS samples showed 820–970 HV and HVOF samples 546–1165 HV, with the highest hardness at DS-T1 (20 N/20 µm) and HVOF-T4 (30 N/30 µm); SEM after scratching showed heterogeneous contrast and crack-like features.
watch_item: The scratch observations are qualitative and do not isolate UNSM-caused damage or establish a definitive scratch-resistance ranking.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
